source.title: In the Shadow of Reasoning: Exploring Behavioral Steering in Large Reasoning Models
source.citation: In the Shadow of Reasoning: Exploring…

record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal-direction extraction and activation interventions in large reasoning models, using a stage-aware, multi-layer steering procedure rather than the original intervention recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper measures refusal-direction geometry and tests refusal/compliance steering, including direction ablation. Results cited from other work are not recorded. It compares several steering variants and baselines; rows below prioritize SubSteer, direction ablation, the Refusal Direction baseline, and measured direction similarities.
record.test_reason: In four reasoning models, it extracts harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal directions and measures refusal and compliance rates under addition, subtraction and direction ablation. This includes the Arditi et al. Refusal Direction baseline. It is a new setting (reasoning models) with direct results on V8 and on V1 in that setting. Extraction position and intervention schedule differ from the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CoT-progress variation dominates reasoning-model activations, leaving the refusal signal subdominant and hard to extract and steer. A pre-decision direction with progress-aware, multi-layer steering gives bidirectional refusal control with little CoT degradation. They add that direction ablation is weaker than subtractive steering on Qwen3.5-9B and GPT-OSS-20B, suggesting compliance may require pushing opposite to vr. They report the same geometry for myopia, survival and power-seeking. They hypothesise post-training shapes the geometry, but do not test this.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful–harmless activation contrasts, but extracts the direction at the pre-decision boundary and applies progress-aware steering across selected layers during CoT. It does not use the original all-layer/all-position ablation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction extraction position changes the measured direction and steering results. Fixed-strength versus progress-aware steering, and single-layer versus multi-layer intervention, also change steering outcomes and CoT unclosed rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal directions extracted at different positions (EOI, pooled CoT, pre-decision) have only moderate pairwise cosine (0.17–0.42). A pooled CoT direction aligns with the CoT-progress direction (cos ≈0.4 on GPT-OSS).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning models the extracted refusal direction depends strongly on extraction position and is confounded with CoT progress.

fits_no_version.finding: CoT-progress variation is 2.34–13.79× larger than the harmful–harmless separation along the refusal direction. Even 0.2×vr at one layer leaves over 60% of Qwen3.5-9B CoTs unclosed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal signal is subdominant during reasoning, giving a narrow effective steering strength.

record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: Evaluation reports success and CoT unclosed rates on 100 jailbreak prompts; broad non-refusal capabilities are not evaluated. No uncertainty intervals or statistical tests are reported for the main steering rates. Direction ablation and compliance steering perform inconsistently across models.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted per-model results for alternative steering-strength and layer-distribution variants (SubSteerfixed and SubSteersingle in Tables 1–2) and other comparison methods in Table 2 (Spherical Steering, PID Steering, Reasoning Manipulation, FPCG). These are comparisons of alternative steering procedures rather than the selected refusal-direction or direction-ablation results recorded above.

untested.parts: Non-reasoning models. All-layer, all-position ablation as in the original. Effects on harmless prompts (inducing refusal on benign instructions). Broad capability preservation; only the CoT unclosed rate is measured.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
Does not test whether jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction, or adversarial training against ablation.
No affine, cone or multi-direction analysis of refusal.
Harmfulness versus refusal encoding not separated.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
Only four 8–20B models. Interventions only during CoT. No harmless-prompt refusal induction and no capability benchmarks.

missing.what: Steering with the EOI direction (the original Arditi extraction position) under the SubSteer schedule. Refusal: 0.68, 0.65, 0.68, 0.93. Compliance: 0.60, 0.61, 0.23, 0.55 (Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek, Qwen3.5, GPT-OSS). This is the closest test of the original direction in reasoning models.
Single-layer large intervention with vr (SubSteersingle). It collapses the CoT on Qwen3.5-9B and GPT-OSS-20B (refusal 0.00, unclosed 1.00). This is the cost of original-style single-layer steering.
Single-layer 0.2×vr on Qwen3.5-9B leaves over 60% of CoTs unclosed; 0.5×vr leaves 99% unclosed.
Pooled CoT direction (vcot) steering: refusal 0.96/0.78/0.98/0.99, but compliance causes high unclosed rates (0.31/0.72 on Qwen models).

record.verdict_notes: Interventions are CoT-only and evaluated on 100 jailbreak prompts. Success requires a naturally closed CoT, so success drops partly reflect CoT disruption rather than refusal behaviour. The RD baseline uses a single selected layer, not the original all-layer ablation. No uncertainty is reported. Table 3 non-refusal behaviours are out of scope.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test projecting one difference-in-means direction out of every layer and position, adding it to harmless prompts, or broad general capabilities. Interventions use a pre-decision direction across selected layers during reasoning.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether attacks work by suppressing the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Compares directions extracted at different positions, but does not test affine or cone models, or establish that a multiple-direction mechanism better explains refusal.
Does not test whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
Tests multiple reasoning model families but not cross-language transfer, transfer between model variants, or base-to-instruct transfer of a direction.
Hypothesizes that post-training shapes the geometry but does not compare training procedures or stages.
Tests refusal-direction measurement and steering in four reasoning models; does not test all components of V1, such as all-layer/all-position ablation or general capability preservation.

conditions.value: example in main text, layer not numerically specified here

rows.operation_detail: Ranks projection coefficients on the pre-decision refusal direction across harmful-refusal, jailbreak-refusal, jailbreak-compliance, and harmless-compliance categories
rows.measure: Mean Kendall rank correlation with expected ordering
rows.note: This is an association measurement, not an intervention result.
rows.check: Correlational only: projection ordering, not an intervention. It cannot show causal mediation (V1).

rows.subject: Four LRMs: Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Qwen3.5-9B, GPT-OSS-20B

rows.note: The paper reports these as evidence that the direction tracks refusal tendency through the CoT.
rows.check: Correlational only (AUROC 0.875); not causal evidence for V1.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Qwen3.5-9B and GPT-OSS-20B compliance steering; fixed-strength single-layer RD addition in all four models
labels.reason: Label right: RD addition reaches 0.65–0.93, Qwen3.5 compliance 0.31, GPT-OSS compliance 0.64 and DA 0.23. But r3 is refusal addition, outside the stated condition group. 'Tops out at 0.76 refusal' overlooks SubSteer with v_cot at 0.98; 0.00 on Qwen3.5-9B (Table 1).

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Direction ablation toward compliance: RD baseline in all four models, and SubSteerDA on Qwen3.5-9B
labels.reason: Compliance does not rise (0.53→0.50, 0.75→0.58, 0.15→0.07, 0.11→0.09; DA Qwen3.5 0.15→0.02), with unclosed up to 0.81. Caveat: RD ablation is applied during CoT only (App. G.3), unlike Arditi's all-position ablation.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Label right. But r13–r16 RD addition does not break the CoT (unclosed 0.00, 0.00, 0.32, 0.00). CoT breakage comes from SubSteer_fixed and SubSteer_single (Table 1) and the intro's 0.2×v_r giving >60% unclosed on Qwen3.5. Capabilities are untested.

relation.reason: Its own add, subtract and ablate results with diff-in-means directions in reasoning models bear directly on whether V1 holds there.

tranche.reason: Four reasoning models are steered during CoT, a new setting. It reports refusal and compliance rates for harmful-minus-harmless diff-in-means directions, including an Arditi RD baseline, so the results bear on V1 and V8. It also argues (T5-like) that the refusal signal is subdominant during CoT.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1–l5 follow the pack's verdict order. In all four models, Table 1 'SubSteer with v_eoi' refusal cells equal Table 2 RD refusal cells (0.68/0.00, 0.65/0.00, 0.68/0.32, 0.93/0.00): possibly duplicated in the paper. There are no uncertainty estimates, no random-direction control and no capability benchmarks. The text carries the standard ICLR reviewer-policy footer, which is addressed to human reviewers.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SubSteer refusal steering on jailbreak prompts across the four tested reasoning models
reader_labels.reason: Refusal success rises in all four models, with the study reporting naturally completed CoTs alongside the refusal outcome (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Compliance steering and activation-space ablation on jailbreak prompts
reader_labels.reason: Compliance results vary across models; direct direction ablation is strong in two models, weak in one, and reverses the expected result in Qwen3.5-9B (r5–r12, r17–r20).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Direction ablation on Qwen3.5-9B jailbreak prompts
reader_labels.reason: Direction ablation reduces compliance success from 0.15 to 0.02 and increases the unclosed rate from 0.26 to 0.46 (r11).
